channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Independence: Historical Lessons for the Present
item.description: Professor Zainidin Kurmanov discusses Kyrgyzstan's path to statehood, emphasizing the importance of remembering historical figures and lessons for the current political elite. He highlights the ancient origins of the Kyrgyz people, citing Chinese chronicles that mention Kyrgyz presence in the 10th century BCE, a claim subject to academic debate.

item.title: UN Secretary-General António Guterres arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has arrived in Kyrgyzstan to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by the Minister of Economy and Commerce, Bakyt Sydykov. Guterres will participate in the Council of Heads of State meeting in Bishkek.

item.title: Twelve Uzbek children left without parental care returned from Russia
item.description: Twelve underage Uzbek citizens, who were left without parental care or were in difficult social situations in various regions of Russia, have been repatriated. The operation was a collaboration between the Uzbek embassy, ministries of internal affairs and health, and the National Agency for Social Protection. Another 22 children are being processed for return.

item.title: Uzbek President congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day, notes strong bilateral ties
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its Independence Day, highlighting the country's economic and social growth. He noted that bilateral relations have reached a new historical stage, becoming allied. Mirziyoyev expressed confidence in the successful hosting of the SCO summit and World Nomad Games.

item.title: Hong Kong banks may finance Tashkent-Samarkand toll road project
item.description: Hong Kong banks are considering financing the construction of the Tashkent-Samarkand toll road. Uzbekistan's Transport Minister and the head of Hong Kong's 'Belt and Road' office discussed potential financial participation. They also explored air travel development and launching direct flights between the two regions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament Speaker congratulates nation on 35th Independence Day
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its 35th Independence Day. He stated that under President Sadyr Japarov's leadership, Kyrgyzstan is entering a new development phase, strengthening its economy and international standing. The hosting of the SCO summit and World Nomad Games signifies the country's growth.

item.title: Kyrgyz State Secretary draws historical parallel between Xi Jinping's visit and Xuanzang's journey
item.description: Kyrgyz State Secretary Arslan Koichiev drew a historical parallel between Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit and the ancient journey of monk Xuanzang. Koichiev noted Xi's stay at a location where Xuanzang had also rested. He referenced Xi's article highlighting historical China-Kyrgyzstan ties and figures like Zhang Qian and Li Bai.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Asked US to Lead Anti-Houthi War, Washington Refused
item.description: Saudi Arabia requested the United States to lead the war against the Houthis, but Washington declined. This issue was raised during a meeting between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Admiral Brad Cooper, head of the US Central Command, on August 14.

item.title: Pope Francis Congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: Pope Francis sent congratulations to Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov and the people on Independence Day. He wished the citizens peace and encouraged their contribution to the common good. The Vatican's Apostolic Nuncio to Kyrgyzstan, Archbishop George Panamthundil, also conveyed wishes for peace and prosperity.

item.title: Items Prohibited at Opening Ceremony of World Nomad Games in Bishkek
item.description: The Ministry of Internal Affairs has published a list of items banned from the 'Bishkek Arena' stadium for the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games. Prohibited items include cigarettes, chewing gum, outside food and drinks, glass bottles, large backpacks, weapons, pyrotechnics, drones, and musical instruments.

item.title: Kazakh President Congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov and the Kyrgyz people on their Independence Day. He highlighted Kyrgyzstan's growing international authority, evidenced by its election to the UN Security Council for 2027-2028. Tokayev also praised the ongoing reforms aimed at economic growth and improving public welfare.

item.title: Shanghai Cooperation Organization's Contribution to Global Governance Initiative
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) celebrates 25 years, having grown into a major international body with 27 member states and a GDP nearing $30 trillion. The SCO has consistently expanded its regional economic cooperation, fostering trade and joint projects in energy, transport, and digital economy. China's active participation in global governance is highlighted, with President Xi Jinping's Global Governance Initiative presented in Tianjin.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Arrives in Bishkek for State Visit and SCO Summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife were welcomed in Bishkek by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and his wife. The leaders reviewed a guard of honor and cultural performances. Xi Jinping conveyed greetings to the Kyrgyz people, noting the strong, stable development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations over 34 years, now a high-level comprehensive partnership. Cooperation is advancing, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project.

item.title: UK Warns Companies Supplying Arms to Ukraine of Russian Attack Risks
item.description: British government officials have informed leaders of defense companies and their staff about an increased threat from the Kremlin. This warning comes as these companies supply arms to Ukraine, making them potential targets for Russian attacks.

item.title: US Strikes Iranian Targets in Strait of Hormuz; Iran Retaliates
item.description: The US conducted strikes on Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, targeting forces preparing to mine the waterway. Iran's IRGC claimed to have retaliated with strikes on two US bases in Jordan. President Trump posted an AI-generated video of explosions on Hark Island.

item.title: New Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk Highway Shows Early Signs of Deterioration
item.description: Activists in the Abai region have reported significant damage to the new Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway, costing over 180 billion tenge. Issues include asphalt damage, foundation settlement, and potential construction quality problems. They seek new inspections and an extended warranty period.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Elevate Strategic Partnership to New Level
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Uzbekistan on August 29-30 for a state visit. Discussions focused on deepening strategic partnership and multifaceted cooperation. Trade turnover exceeded $1 billion last year, and the number of joint ventures has increased sevenfold.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses SCO Summit on Economic Cooperation and Infrastructure
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will attend the SCO summit in Bishkek on August 31-September 1. The summit marks the organization's 25th anniversary and aims to advance economic, transport, and anti-crisis agendas. Leaders from 21 countries, including China, Russia, and India, are expected to participate.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister's State Visit to Uzbekistan Concludes with Signed Agreements
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi concluded his state visit to Uzbekistan on August 29-30. High-level talks focused on deepening strategic partnership and cooperation in trade, energy, health, and other sectors. A significant package of bilateral agreements was signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India aim to reach $5 billion trade volume by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have agreed to increase their trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030. Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Bishkek for the SCO summit and the World Nomad Games.

item.title: Uzbek President to attend SCO summit and World Nomad Games in Bishkek
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Bishkek on August 31-September 1 for the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting and an "SCO plus" format meeting. Discussions will cover cooperation, security, economy, and transport. Mirziyoyev will also attend the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games.

item.title: Homage Paid to Lal Bahadur Shastri's Memory in Tashkent
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accompanied by Uzbek Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov, laid flowers at the monument to Lal Bahadur Shastri in Tashkent. The visit highlights the strong historical and diplomatic ties between India and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Putin and Pashinyan to Discuss Armenia's EU vs EAEU Choice in Bishkek
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan will meet in Bishkek to discuss Armenia's future integration course and a potential referendum on the matter. The Kremlin stated that the decision rests with the Armenian people. Moscow views a referendum as a possible path for Armenia's integration choice.

item.title: Kyrgyz Official Sees Historical Echoes in Xi Jinping's Visit, Recalling Xuanzang
item.description: Kyrgyz State Secretary Arslan Koichiev drew a symbolic historical parallel between Chinese President Xi Jinping's current state visit and the journey of the monk Xuanzang in Central Asia nearly 1,400 years ago. Koichiev noted Xi's stop at Bas-Böltök, the same location Xuanzang reportedly rested.

item.title: Uzbek President and Indian Prime Minister Plant Tree at Guest of Honor Avenue
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi planted a tree together at the Guest of Honor Avenue of the Kuksaroy residence. This ceremony symbolized the commencement of a new phase in Uzbek-Indian multifaceted relations and commitment to strengthening bilateral friendship.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Arrives in Bishkek for SCO Summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Kyrgyzstan's capital, Bishkek, for a working visit. He will attend the SCO Heads of State Council meeting, an 'SCO plus' format meeting, and the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games. Modi was previously in Tashkent for a state visit to Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Leaders Conclude Talks, Elevating Partnership
item.description: Leaders of Uzbekistan and India reviewed their talks, highlighting strong friendship and mutual respect. India is recognized as a strategic partner, with achievements in digital technology noted. Bilateral relations have reached a comprehensive strategic partnership level.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Sadyr Japarov Holds Informal Meeting with China's Xi Jinping in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov and Chinese President Xi Jinping held an informal meeting in Bishkek, accompanied by their spouses. The leaders discussed cooperation issues and key agenda items for upcoming official events in a cordial atmosphere.

item.title: Mongolian President Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Plus Meeting and World Nomad Games
item.description: Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit. He will attend the SCO Plus high-level meeting and the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games. The president was presented with a snow leopard toy, the symbol of the games.

item.title: Most Decorated Olympic Wrestler Arrives in Bishkek for World Nomad Games
item.description: Mijaín López Núñez, a five-time Olympic Greco-Roman wrestling champion and the most decorated wrestler in Olympic history, has arrived in Kyrgyzstan. He is an honorary guest of the World Alysh Federation for the World Nomad Games. Núñez recently won his fifth Olympic title at the Paris Olympics.

item.title: Meat Imported from India to Uzbekistan Will Be Prepared Under Halal Certification
item.description: Meat imported from India to Uzbekistan will be prepared under halal certification. The Minister of Agriculture announced agreements on the participation of Uzbek specialists in meat preparation and slaughter processes in India, ensuring international and halal certifications.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Sign Package of Documents to Strengthen Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and India signed a package of documents aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation after high-level talks between Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The documents cover trade, economy, investment, culture, education, environment, and tourism.

item.title: Uzbekistan Awards Indian Prime Minister Modi with Friendship Order
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has awarded Indian Prime Minister Narendra Damodardas Modi the "Oliy Darajali Do'stlik" Order. The award recognizes Modi's significant contributions to strengthening historical friendship and strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and India, as well as deepening multifaceted cooperation.

item.title: Analyst: Kazakh and Russian Presidents Unhappy with Current World Order
item.description: Political analyst Arkady Dubnov suggests that Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Russian President Vladimir Putin are dissatisfied with the current global situation. Dubnov notes Tokayev's disappointment with declining international trust and the UN Security Council's ineffectiveness, while Putin expresses bitterness over unmet expectations.

item.title: Uzbekistan's 35 Years: Path Towards Open Dialogue Between State and Society
item.description: Uzbekistan marks 35 years of independence, reflecting on its path, achievements, and future strategies. Professor Sanjar Saidov discusses the country's role in the international arena and the evolution of its media landscape since 2016, noting increased pluralism and changes in media practice despite existing legal frameworks.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Awarded Uzbekistan's Highest State Honor
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi received Uzbekistan's Order of "Oliy Darajali Doʻstlik" in Tashkent. The award recognizes India's development and Modi's contribution to strengthening Uzbek-Indian friendship. The visit concluded with an agreement to elevate bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership.

item.title: Russia preparing massive strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities, says Defense Ministry
item.description: Russia is reportedly preparing for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities. The Defense Ministry stated this measure is a response to Kyiv's ongoing attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure and its fuel and energy complex. Further details were not provided.

item.title: Uzbekistan President and Indian Prime Minister agree to elevate relations
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi met to advance strategic partnership and multifaceted cooperation. Bilateral trade exceeded $1 billion last year, and joint ventures have increased sevenfold. The leaders noted the growing educational and cultural ties, with four Indian universities operating in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev to attend SCO summit events in Bishkek
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Bishkek on August 31-September 1 for the upcoming SCO Council of Heads of State meeting and an "SCO Plus" format meeting. Discussions will focus on developing multifaceted cooperation within the SCO and improving its activities. Bilateral meetings are also planned.

item.title: Tashkent region and Anhui province expand cooperation in agriculture
item.description: The Tashkent region and China's Anhui province are broadening their cooperation, particularly in agriculture. Discussions focused on joint projects in water-saving technologies, smart greenhouses, and developing climate-resilient crop varieties. The regions have established sister-city relations and are exploring agrobiotechnology and personnel training.
